Bodies a step sends or answers with: JSON bodies and payloads, `respond:` text and JSON bodies, status and header values, and `run: email` html.

**JSON bodies and room payloads keep each value whole.** A `run: webhook` `body:`, a `run: api` text `body:` (or `json:` written as text) or a legacy `ws:` `payload:` written as a JSON document has each `${{ }}` value JSON-escaped inside a string literal and written as exactly one JSON value elsewhere: JSON text (a json_group_array() column) or a number stays as is, a null value is null and anything else becomes a JSON string (a reference with no value at all fails an api or webhook step before anything is sent); a string the caller sent is a JSON string even when it is JSON text of an object or array (json_value_typing). A `:name` is substituted only inside a string literal (outside one, `:` is the key separator). A request value cannot add or override keys, and a quote or newline does not break the JSON. Other templates (plain text, a lone `${{ x }}`) render verbatim.

**Body, status and header values a step sends.** (1) `run: webhook` `with.payload` (a map or list), or `with.body` written as a map or list, is the JSON body, each `${{ }}` value resolved like an api `json:` value; a value that does not resolve stops the step before anything is sent, and a payload carrying an env value or one derived from env may not go to a request-chosen URL. `body:` and `payload:` together are refused. (2) `run: respond` `with.status` written as `${{ }}` or quoted (`"404"`) is rendered: an integer 200-599 is the status, anything else fails the step with a 500 (`respond status rendered to "x", want 200-599`). (3) `run: api` `with.body` written as a map or list, and `with.json` written as a list, are sent as JSON (Content-Type application/json unless the step's `headers:` set one). Next to `json:` or `form:` a map `body:` is refused. (4) `run: respond` `with.headers` and `with.content_type` are sent, through an allowlist (respond_headers below). (5) `run: email` `with.unsubscribe_url` becomes an optional HTTPS `List-Unsubscribe` header. Native RFC 8058 POST is explicit opt-in with `unsubscribe_one_click: true` (or a true/false template), and requires a valid HTTPS URL without fragments or userinfo. Email also supports `cc`/`bcc` with the same recipient expansion, total limit and delivery policy as `to`; BCC stays out of headers. See the email topic for unsubscribe endpoint requirements and ordinary-header failure behavior.

**`respond:` text bodies.** A string `body:` is typed from your template with its refs removed: `

Hello ${{ user.first_name }}

` is text/html, `${{ params.q }} not found` is text/plain, so a request value at the start of a text body cannot make it an HTML page. A body that is exactly one reference answers application/json, a text value as a JSON string (declare `content_type:` to send the text itself, see respond_headers → content_type); a body made of several refs and no text of your own is typed from the rendered bytes but is never served as HTML or XML. Values are not HTML-escaped in a text body; return JSON (`json:`) for data, and escape anything you place in an HTML body yourself.

**respond JSON emits native types.** A whole-value ref - `years: "${{ steps.calc.outputs.years }}"` - that resolves to an array or object is emitted as REAL JSON (`[2025,2026]` / `{...}`), and a scalar as its native number/bool, at ANY nesting depth. So a compute step can return `{years:[...], ebitda:[...], irr: 0.08}` and you map each field straight into the response - no need to JSON-stringify-and-parse-client-side. (A ref EMBEDDED in a larger string, e.g. `"total: ${{ x }}"`, still renders as text - only whole-value refs go native.) A whole-value ref whose LAST pipe yields a whole number - `| length`, `| count`, `| cents` - is a JSON number too: `n: ${{ steps.x.outputs.rows | length }}` answers `"n": 20`. Every other pipe returns text (`| number` and `| currency` format for display, `| digits` keeps leading zeros), as does a chain ending in `| default:` or using a `||` fallback. api `json:`, webhook `payload:` and broadcast payloads resolve the same way.

**`run: email` inline `html:` escapes values.** A `${{ }}` or `:name` value in an email step's `html:` is escaped for the HTML context it lands in (entity-escaped in text and attributes; a script-capable scheme is removed from href/src), exactly like a `template:` file, so a request field cannot add links or markup to mail sent from your domain. Markup on purpose: `${{{ steps.build.outputs.html }}}` (sanitized) or `${{{{ ... }}}}` (as is; only for HTML your own steps produced), and a markdown pipe's output stays HTML. Also written as is: an `html:` that is exactly one reference (`html: "${{ steps.build.outputs.html }}"` - the value is the whole document your steps built), an env value (`${{ env.FOOTER_HTML }}`), and a reference whose last pipe is `raw` (`${{ steps.build.outputs.table | raw }}`); `| raw` changes nothing anywhere else. `| nl2br` escapes the value first and then turns its newlines into `
`. `text:`, `subject:`, `to:` stay plain text.
